subject: jutil: allocation-free fast paths found by the parse benchmark
areas: internal/jutil preconditions.go, collections.go; parser line_number_scanner.go; parsebench
what: Adds Guava-style fixed-arity Preconditions (CheckStateMsg1..3, CheckArgumentMsg1..3, CheckNotNullMsg1..2) that box only on failure; StringFromUTF16 allocates once; StringToUTF16 ASCII fast path; ArrayList bounds-failure path moved out of line so Get inlines.
measured_effect: parse benchmark (14,690-file corpus) 8.3-9.5 s -> 6.6-6.8 s per pass; allocated 3.1 GB -> 2.6 GB; variadic CheckArgumentMsg boxing was 8% of time
mech_form: Emit fixed-arity Preconditions calls (1-3 template args) that box only on the failure path, mirroring Guava overloads. allowed part: RUNTIME ASCII fast path in UTF-16 conversion helpers and out-of-line bounds failure in ArrayList.Get.

subject: Use fixed-arity Preconditions at every 1-3 argument call site
areas: internal/rhino node.go, ir.go, prop_translator.go; internal/colors; PORTING.md
what: gofmt -r mechanical rewrite of 67 variadic Preconditions call sites to the fixed-arity forms; PORTING.md gains the allocation rules.
mech_form: Same rule as 2778cc1f: choose the fixed-arity Preconditions overload at every 1-3 argument call site (this commit was literally a gofmt -r rewrite, so it is also expressible as a post-flip tool).
notes: Call-site half of 2778cc1f; no separate measurement.

subject: jutil: StringBuilder.insert shifts the tail in place
areas: internal/jutil stringbuilder.go; affects jscomp CodePrinter compact printer
what: StringBuilder.Insert/InsertChar shift the tail in place with amortized growth instead of copying the whole buffer per insert (was quadratic allocation for line-break insertion).
mech_form: Runtime StringBuilder emulation: insert must shift in place over an amortized-growth buffer as Java AbstractStringBuilder does.
notes: Undoes an inefficiency of the hand-written runtime; no numbers stated.

subject: jscomp: printer allocations — StringBuilder(1024), no *string per mapped node, reused UTF-16 scratch
areas: internal/jscomp code_generator.go (StrEscape, EscapeUnrecognizedCharacters), code_printer.go (MappedCodePrinter.StartSourceMapping)
what: Printer StringBuilder starts at capacity 1024; StartSourceMapping tests GetStaticSourceFile()!=nil instead of GetSourceFileName() which allocated a *string per node; StrEscape reuses a UTF-16 scratch buffer for ASCII strings.
measured_effect: source-map printing of a 2.3 MB file: 125 ms -> 71 ms
mech_form: Lower @Nullable String returns to string plus sentinel/ok instead of a freshly allocated *string, so null tests do not allocate. allowed part: RUNTIME charAt access over ASCII strings without a UTF-16 copy (or scratch reuse); inferred: StringBuilder(1024) capacity is whatever the Java source passes.

subject: perf: Compiler.CodeBuilder.append counts lines in one pass
areas: internal/jscomp compiler.go Compiler.CodeBuilder.append
what: Line/column counting in CodeBuilder.append scans the WTF-8 bytes once for newline instead of looping StringIndexOfCharFrom, which converted the whole string to UTF-16 per call (O(lines x size)).
measured_effect: downlevel-whitespace wall 7.41 s -> 2.62 s (CPU 11.09 s -> 3.40 s); downlevel-simple 17.60 s -> 11.96 s (CPU 16.45 s -> 11.41 s)
mech_form: String.indexOf(char, from) in the string runtime must not convert the string per call (byte search for ASCII chars, see 6e6407af); then the faithful Java loop is linear and no hand edit of CodeBuilder is needed.
notes: Root cause fixed generally in 6e6407af; the inefficiency was introduced by the hand port string representation.

subject: perf: memoize Color.hashCode
areas: internal/colors color.go; jscomp DisambiguateProperties
what: Memoizes Color.hashCode in the Color object because the Go immutable sets recompute (and box) their hash on every call, unlike Guava ImmutableSet/String which cache theirs.
measured_effect: typed-app disambiguateProperties 2586 ms -> 393 ms; whole task wall 16.40 s -> 14.64 s, CPU 19.20 s -> 16.29 s
mech_form: Runtime ImmutableSet (and string-keyed sets) cache their hashCode as Guava does and hash String elements without boxing; then the translated AutoValue hashCode is cheap without a hand memo. Alternatively a translator rule memoizing hashCode of AutoValue classes whose fields are all final.
notes: The hand memo in Color itself would be a pass/class-specific edit; the general form is the runtime cache.

subject: perf(jutil): cache compiled Patterns by regex
areas: internal/jutil pattern.go; affects CompilerOptions init, CheckDuplicateCase, CodePrinter.Builder
what: Pattern_Compile caches successful compilations by regex string (bounded at 4096), returning distinct *Pattern objects sharing the immutable compiled RE2 programs.
measured_effect: checks-only suspiciousCode 2699 ms -> 1212 ms; whole task wall 22.24 s -> 20.93 s, CPU 23.70 s -> 21.21 s
mech_form: Runtime java.util.regex.Pattern emulation keeps a bounded cache of compiled programs keyed by regex+flags.

subject: perf(jutil): byte-level fast paths for String compareTo and hashCode
areas: internal/jutil jstring.go (StringCompareTo, StringHashCode, isASCII); affects rhino PropertyMap TreeMap probes
what: String.compareTo compares bytes and falls back to UTF-16 only when the first difference is inside a non-ASCII character; hashCode hashes in one pass without converting; isASCII checks 8 bytes at a time.
measured_effect: checks-only wall 19.79 s -> 18.85 s (CPU 20.13 s -> 19.76 s); typed-app wall 14.97 s -> 13.79 s (CPU 14.95 s -> 14.54 s)
mech_form: String runtime helpers: byte-level compareTo and one-pass Java hashCode over UTF-8/WTF-8 storage with a UTF-16 fallback.

subject: perf: decode protos without copying embedded messages
areas: internal/jscomp proto_runtime.go, serialization_typed_ast_deserializer.go
what: Proto reader aliases the input buffer for embedded messages, strings and skipped fields instead of copying per nesting level; the runtime-library TypedAST resource is read at its known size instead of io.ReadAll.
measured_effect: 25 single-file compiles x2 total wall: 25.18 s -> 24.47 s (proto reader), 23.91 s -> 23.47 s (sized read)
mech_form: Protobuf wire codec: sub-message and string decoding slice the immutable input buffer (zero-copy) and only kept bytes fields are copied; resource streams read at known length.

subject: perf: JSDocInfo.getSuppressions allocates only when there are some
areas: internal/rhino js_doc_info.go JSDocInfo.getSuppressions; jscomp JSDocSerializer
what: Returns one shared empty set when there are no suppressions (Java returns the ImmutableSet.of() singleton) and returns the built set without a second copy.
measured_effect: 25 single-file compiles x2: wall 23.29 s -> 23.21 s, CPU 20.96 s -> 20.42 s
mech_form: Runtime immutable collections: ImmutableSet.of()/ImmutableList.of() return shared empty singletons and copyOf of an already-immutable collection returns it unchanged, as Guava does.
notes: Undoes a hand-port inefficiency.

subject: perf(jutil): CharStreams.toString of an unread InputStreamReader
areas: internal/jutil input_stream_reader.go CharStreams_ToString; builtin externs loading
what: CharStreams.toString of a not-yet-read InputStreamReader returns the decoded text directly when it is valid UTF-8 instead of round-tripping through UTF-16 chunks.
measured_effect: one small SIMPLE compile, 30 runs: wall 971 ms -> 941 ms, CPU 901 ms -> 879 ms
mech_form: I/O runtime: Reader implementations expose a whole-remaining-text fast path used by CharStreams.toString.

subject: perf(jutil): StringReader converts to UTF-16 on its first read
areas: internal/jutil input_stream_reader.go (StringReader), gson_json_reader.go
what: StringReader defers its UTF-16 conversion to the first read, and CharStreams_ToString returns an unread StringReader string directly.
measured_effect: with next commit, typed-app allocation 1961 MB -> 1759 MB per run; wall 14.65 s -> 14.33 s for this commit
mech_form: I/O runtime: lazy UTF-16 view in StringReader plus the same unread-reader fast path in CharStreams.toString.

subject: perf: JsFileLineParser drains its reader with CharStreams.toString
areas: internal/jscomp deps_js_file_line_parser.go (Go-only newBufferedReader adapter)
what: The Go-only reader adapter in JsFileLineParser drains through CharStreams_ToString instead of UTF-16 chunks into a growing buffer (about 140 MB garbage for 971 files).
measured_effect: with previous commit typed-app allocation 1961 MB -> 1759 MB per run; wall alone 14.55 s -> 15.16 s (stated as noise), CPU 14.62 s -> 14.74 s
mech_form: BufferedReader/readLine in the I/O runtime reads lines from the backing string without converting the whole text to UTF-16 and back.
notes: The slow adapter was a hand-port artefact; commit states no wall gain on its own.

subject: perf(jutil): String indexOf/lastIndexOf(char) without converting
areas: internal/jutil jstring.go StringIndexOfCharFrom, StringLastIndexOfCharFrom; callers GlobalNamespace, NodeUtil, QualifiedName, ProcessCommonJSModules
what: indexOf/lastIndexOf(char) no longer convert the whole string to UTF-16 per call: for an ASCII char they search bytes (indexOf skips to fromIndex by code point), removing quadratic loops and a copy per step.
measured_effect: microbenchmark indexOf loop over 10 KB non-ASCII text: 24.5 ms, 8.7 MB, 401 allocs -> 2.1 ms, 0 allocs; whole tasks no measurable change (checks-only 20.04 s -> 20.39 s)
mech_form: String runtime: char search helpers operate on the stored bytes for ASCII needles with index translation, UTF-16 fallback otherwise.

subject: perf: Compiler.CodeBuilder.endsWith converts only the tail
areas: internal/jscomp compiler.go Compiler.CodeBuilder.endsWith
what: endsWith copies only the tail units of the StringBuilder instead of converting the whole output buffer to a string and taking a substring (was quadratic in output size with PRINT_INPUT_DELIMITER).
measured_effect: downlevel-whitespace with --formatting=PRINT_INPUT_DELIMITER: 6.18 s -> 3.38 s (CPU 6.29 s -> 3.24 s)
mech_form: A faithful translation of sb.substring(start) calls the runtime StringBuilder.Substring(start), which copies only the tail; the hand port had written String() followed by substring.
notes: Bench tasks do not use this flag.

subject: perf(jutil): flat collection iterators, ToSlice sized up front
areas: internal/jutil collections.go (LinkedHashMap/Set, ObjectLinkedHashMap/Set), java_hash_map.go, java_hash_set.go, tree_set.go, treemap.go
what: Keys/Values/All iterators walk entries directly as flat iter.Seq functions that inline into the caller loop (were nested escaping closures, 7 allocations per range); ToSlice/KeySlice allocate once at the collection size.
measured_effect: typed-app 48.8M mallocs / 2038 MB -> 40.9M / 1855 MB; typed-app wall 12.21 s -> 11.89 s (CPU 15.25 s -> 14.26 s); checks-only wall 17.22 s -> 16.56 s (CPU 20.74 s -> 20.25 s)
mech_form: Collections runtime: every iterator is a single non-nested range-over-func that the compiler can inline (no escaping closure), and toArray/copy helpers presize the result.

subject: perf: RhinoStringPool interns through a strong map, not unique.Make
areas: internal/rhino rhino_string_pool.go
what: RhinoStringPool.addOrGet uses a mutex-guarded map[string]string (reset at 2^20 entries) instead of unique.Make, which cost a concurrent-trie lookup, weak pointer conversion and a post-GC cleanup walk.
measured_effect: parsebench runner wall 13.35 s -> 12.31 s, CPU 15.26 s -> 13.67 s; checks-only wall 16.69 s -> 16.07 s (CPU 20.37 s -> 19.24 s); typed-app wall 11.52 s -> 11.34 s (CPU 14.10 s -> 13.66 s); unique.Make was ~14% of front-end CPU
mech_form: String pool runtime component: the Guava weak interner is implemented as a strong map[string]string (locked or per-thread) rather than unique.Make.
notes: A single mutex here would contend under parallel parsing (relevant to PARSE-PAR).

subject: perf(jutil): Slab, a chunk allocator for objects that die together
areas: internal/jutil slab.go
what: Adds jutil.Slab[T], a chunk allocator (16/32/64/128-element chunks) handing out pointers to zeroed T for objects that die together.
mech_form: The Slab type itself is a small runtime component, but it gives no gain until wired into specific allocation sites, and that wiring needs hand lifetime reasoning (see fd5954e5: NOT-ALLOWED).
notes: Enabler only; measurements are in fd5954e5.

subject: perf(parser): tokens, their positions and tree ranges come from slabs
areas: internal/parser scanner.go, line_number_scanner.go, parser.go, identifier_token.go
what: Scanner tokens, their SourcePositions/SourceRanges and parse-tree ranges are allocated from per-parse jutil.Slabs via Go-only helpers; comments keep plain allocation because their positions outlive the parse.
measured_effect: parsebench runner CPU 13.00 s -> 11.80 s, wall 13.58 s -> 10.99 s; parser mode CPU 7.09 s -> 6.12 s, wall 8.19 s -> 7.21 s; checks-only CPU 18.52 s -> 18.22 s; 30 single-file compiles x2 CPU 19.81 s -> 19.51 s; +~7% bytes allocated from partly used chunks; these objects were 61% of front-end allocations
mech_form: algorithmic: slab wiring chosen by hand lifetime reasoning (tokens die after IRFactory, comment positions must not be slabbed). allowed part: a TRANSLATOR rule lowering small final immutable classes (SourcePosition, SourceRange) to value structs embedded in their owner would remove most of the same allocations without lifetime analysis.

subject: perf: TokenStream.isKeyword converts only non-ASCII names to UTF-16
areas: internal/rhino token_stream.go TokenStream.isKeyword; called by IRFactory per NAME
what: isKeyword copies a short (<=12) ASCII name into a stack buffer and skips conversion for longer ASCII names instead of always converting to a heap UTF-16 slice (94% of front-end StringToUTF16 calls).
measured_effect: parsebench runner CPU 11.90 s -> 11.46 s, wall 16.46 s -> 15.03 s, allocated 4592 MB -> 4530 MB per corpus pass
mech_form: String runtime: charAt/length on ASCII strings read bytes in place (no UTF-16 copy), so the translated charAt switch needs no conversion; free if jsgo-mech strings are already UTF-16 indexable.
notes: Hand edit in jsgo; the general form is the runtime charAt fast path.

subject: perf(jutil): small LinkedHashMaps without a Go map, sets hold their map
areas: internal/jutil collections.go (LinkedHashMap, ObjectLinkedHashMap, LinkedHashSet, ObjectLinkedHashSet)
what: LinkedHashMap/ObjectLinkedHashMap build their Go map index only above 8 entries (linear scan of the entry list below that); ObjectLinkedHashMap buckets chain through a field; sets hold their map by value (one allocation).
measured_effect: allocation per run: typed-app 38.4M mallocs / 1776 MB -> 33.2M / 1473 MB; checks-only 52.9M / 2757 MB -> 50.0M / 2533 MB; downlevel-simple 28.1M / 1528 MB -> 24.1M / 1297 MB; CPU typed-app 13.44 s -> 12.24 s, checks-only 18.48 s -> 17.06 s, downlevel-simple 9.95 s -> 9.22 s; 49.5% of 1.43M LinkedHashMaps stay empty, 98.4% hold <= 8
mech_form: Collections runtime: small-size mode for insertion-ordered hash maps/sets (no hash index until > 8 entries, lazy allocation when empty) and sets embedding their map by value.

subject: perf(jutil): ObjectsEqualsOf/ObjectHashCodeOf compare String keys unboxed
areas: internal/jutil objects.go (ObjectsEqualsOf, ObjectHashCodeOf), collections.go ObjectLinkedHashMap
what: Generic helpers take the type parameter directly and handle string and int in a type switch without converting to an interface (no boxing, no reflective string compare); ObjectLinkedHashMap lookups use them.
measured_effect: allocation per run: typed-app 33.24M mallocs / 1473 MB -> 32.81M / 1466 MB; checks-only 50.01M / 2533 MB -> 49.40M / 2524 MB; wall/CPU within noise
mech_form: Collections runtime: generic equals/hashCode helpers parameterised on K with unboxed fast paths for string and integer keys.

subject: perf: HamtPMap hashes and compares String keys without boxing them
areas: internal/rhino hamt_p_map.go; affects LinkedFlowScope (type inference), JSTypeRegistry
what: HamtPMap key comparison and hash use the type-parameter helpers (ObjectsEqualsOf, direct String hash) instead of boxing the key into an interface per probe.
measured_effect: allocation per run: typed-app 32.81M mallocs / 1466 MB -> 32.45M / 1461 MB; checks-only 49.40M / 2524 MB -> 48.38M / 2508 MB; typed-app CPU 13.69 s -> 13.26 s (three commits together), checks-only 19.02 s -> 19.45 s (noise)
mech_form: When Objects.equals/hashCode/key.equals/key.hashCode is applied to a value of generic type K, emit the generic unboxed runtime helper (EqualsOf[K]/HashCodeOf[K]) instead of converting the operand to any.
notes: Also relevant to CHECKS (LinkedFlowScope slot lookups).

subject: perf: JSIdentifier.isJSIdentifier reads short ASCII names in place
areas: internal/rhino js_identifier.go; called from NodeUtil.getBestLValueName in TypedScopeCreator
what: isJSIdentifier copies ASCII strings up to 64 bytes into a stack buffer instead of converting to a heap UTF-16 slice.
measured_effect: allocation per run: typed-app 32.45M mallocs -> 32.42M; checks-only 48.38M / 2508 MB -> 47.72M / 2497 MB
mech_form: Same as 4ee930b4: charAt/length over ASCII strings read in place by the string runtime, no UTF-16 heap copy.

subject: perf(jutil): LinkedHashMap marks removed entries by prev == self
areas: internal/jutil collections.go LinkedHashMap entry
what: Removed-entry flag replaced by prev pointing at the entry itself, shrinking set and pointer-keyed map entries from 48 to 32 bytes.
measured_effect: allocated per run: typed-app 1460 MB -> 1431 MB; checks-only 2497 MB -> 2439 MB; downlevel-simple 1294 MB -> 1278 MB; wall/CPU within noise
mech_form: Collections runtime: linked hash entry without a separate tombstone bool (self-pointing prev) so entries fit a 32-byte size class.

subject: perf(rhino): Node's traversal fields lead and pack into 32 bytes
areas: internal/rhino node.go Node struct
what: Reorders Node fields: the two int32 fields share the first word, followed by next, first, parent, previous; Node shrinks 152 -> 144 bytes and the hot traversal fields sit in one cache line for 3 of 4 nodes.
measured_effect: typed-app CPU 12.94 s -> 12.56 s; downlevel-simple CPU 9.46 s -> 9.14 s; checks-only CPU 18.27 s -> 17.56 s; allocation typed-app 1431 -> 1423 MB, checks-only 2439 -> 2416 MB, downlevel-simple 1278 -> 1271 MB
mech_form: Struct field ordering rule: pack sub-word fields together and place fields by size; hot-fields-first for Node needs a per-class ordering hint, or belongs to the handwritten node store (RUNTIME) if Node lives there.

subject: perf: CodePrinter.Builder makes its default CompilerOptions lazily
areas: internal/jscomp code_printer.go CodePrinter.Builder; affects Compiler.toSource, CheckDuplicateCase
what: CodePrinter.Builder creates its default CompilerOptions lazily in getOptions instead of eagerly in the constructor (callers almost always replace it immediately); a CompilerOptions costs ~100 allocations in Go.
measured_effect: allocation per run: checks-only 47.72M mallocs / 2416 MB -> 45.52M / 2274 MB; typed-app 32.41M / 1423 MB -> 32.27M / 1413 MB; downlevel-simple 23.96M / 1271 MB -> 23.79M / 1259 MB; checks-only CPU 18.44 s -> 16.96 s (median of 4) and 17.88 s -> 17.46 s (median of 3)
mech_form: algorithmic: hand-made lazy initialisation of one class field, requiring knowledge that construction has no side effect. allowed part: make new CompilerOptions() cheap through the runtime (Pattern cache 4f7a3728, lazily allocated/small collections 46219a0a).

subject: perf(rhino): Node.PropListItem packs into 32 bytes
areas: internal/rhino node.go Node.PropListItem
what: Reorders PropListItem fields so the byte, bool and int32 share one word: 40 -> 32 bytes (48 -> 32 byte size class).
measured_effect: with next commit, allocated bytes: typed-app 1413 MB -> 1408 MB, checks-only 2274 MB -> 2267 MB, downlevel-simple 1259 MB -> 1254 MB
mech_form: Order struct fields by decreasing size/alignment so sub-word fields share a word (or node-store runtime if property lists live there).

subject: perf(rhino): type checkers' nullable settings point at shared values
areas: internal/rhino jstype_equality_checker.go, jstype_subtype_checker.go
what: Nullable enum/Boolean fields set by EqualityChecker.setEqMethod and SubtypeChecker setters point into shared tables of the possible values instead of a fresh heap copy of the argument (1.1M allocations in checks-only).
measured_effect: mallocs per run (with previous commit): checks-only 45.52M -> 44.45M; typed-app 32.27M -> 31.96M
mech_form: Lower nullable enum / boxed Boolean fields to a value type with a null sentinel (e.g. zero = unset, tri-state bool) rather than a pointer to a copied value.
notes: Completed by 4109a142 (escape of the parameter).

subject: perf: getQualifiedName and getBestLValueName return without boxing
areas: internal/rhino node.go Node.getQualifiedName, getQualifiedNameForGetProp; internal/jscomp node_util.go NodeUtil.getBestLValueName
what: getQualifiedName/getBestLValueName bodies return (string, ok) with an inlinable *string wrapper so the header stays on the caller stack; GETPROP chains build the name in one presized byte slice instead of a heap strings.Builder.
measured_effect: allocation per run: checks-only 44.45M mallocs / 2266 MB -> 39.97M / 2179 MB; typed-app 31.96M / 1407 MB -> 30.06M / 1371 MB; downlevel-simple 23.79M / 1254 MB -> 22.55M / 1232 MB; checks-only CPU 16.76 s -> 16.34 s (with next commit); these were 12% of checks-only allocations
mech_form: Lower @Nullable String returns to (string, ok) or string with sentinel instead of *string. allowed part: POSTFLIP-TOOL/translator rule replacing a non-escaping StringBuilder local by a presized byte buffer.
notes: The presized single-buffer GETPROP builder is a small hand rewrite of one method (inferred: not derivable by a general rule beyond the non-escaping builder).

subject: perf(rhino): type checkers' setters stop moving their argument to the heap
areas: internal/rhino jstype_equality_checker.go, jstype_subtype_checker.go
what: The fallback branch of the checker setters copies the argument into a branch-local variable so taking its address no longer forces the parameter to the heap on every call.
measured_effect: allocation per run: checks-only 39.97M mallocs / 2179 MB -> 36.79M / 2167 MB; typed-app 30.06M / 1371 MB -> 29.02M / 1366 MB; downlevel-simple unchanged; checks-only CPU 16.76 s -> 16.34 s (with previous commit); typed-app 11.41 s -> 11.44 s (noise)
mech_form: Same rule as b7fd5330: nullable enum/Boolean as value plus sentinel removes the address-of-parameter escape entirely; in general never emit &param for boxing, copy to a local in the boxing branch.
notes: Follow-up completing b7fd5330 (missed escape, not a behaviour bug).

subject: perf(rhino): Node packs into 96 bytes; rarely set fields move to node_ext
areas: internal/rhino node.go
what: rhino.Node shrinks from 144 to 96 bytes: StringNode.str and TemplateLiteralSubstringNode.raw share one field, rarely set payloads (originalName, number, bigint, cooked) move to a lazily allocated node_ext, length becomes int32 next to the kind byte; the 32 hot bytes fit one cache line.
measured_effect: Peak RSS checks-only 768 -> 660 MB, typed-app 275 -> 246 MB; alloc checks-only 2167 -> 2100 MB (mallocs 36.79M -> 36.86M); CPU downlevel-simple median 8.52 s -> 8.19 s, checks-only 15.89 s -> 15.61 s
mech_form: Node store layout: keep only hot fields (token, position, links) in the main record and put rarely set payloads (original name, number/bigint/cooked values) in a side table or lazily allocated extension; narrow length to int32.
notes: Java Node is 56-64 B; the hand port had folded all subclass payloads into every node.

subject: perf: TypeInference's flow brancher keeps its fields in one variable
areas: internal/jscomp type_inference.go; TypeInference createFlowBrancher
what: The anonymous FlowBrancher kept its three fields as three separately captured (and so separately heap-allocated) closure variables; they are now one struct variable, halving allocations per brancher (4 -> 2).
measured_effect: checks-only 36.86M mallocs / 2100 MB -> 36.43M / 2097 MB
mech_form: Lower an anonymous class / lambda with mutable state to one environment struct holding all its fields (one allocation), never to several individually captured-by-reference Go variables.
notes: CPU measured only together with the next three commits (see eba38339).

subject: perf: TypeValidator reuses its WellFormedTemplatizedTypeVerifier
areas: internal/jscomp type_validator.go; TypeCheck expectWellFormedTemplatizedType
what: TypeValidator keeps one spare WellFormedTemplatizedTypeVerifier visitor and re-points it at the node per call (allocating a new one only on re-entrancy) instead of allocating a visitor for every visited node.
measured_effect: checks-only 36.43M mallocs / 2097 MB -> 35.06M / 2055 MB (visitor was 4% of checks-only allocations); typed-app 29.24M / 1348 MB -> 28.80M / 1336 MB (with previous commit)
mech_form: Pattern rewrite: `new V(args).visit(x)` where V is a stateless-after-call visitor that is not stored anywhere -> stack value or a take/put spare instance on the owner; needs only an escape/storage check, not pass knowledge.
notes: Borderline: the spare-instance scheme was written by hand; a tool must prove the visitor is never retained.

subject: perf: graph nodes hold their edge lists; jutil.ArrayList.InitWithBuffer
areas: internal/jscomp graph_linked_directed_graph.go; internal/jutil collections.go (ArrayList.InitWithBuffer); all CFGs
what: LinkedDiGraphNode embeds its in/out edge ArrayLists by value with a one-element inline backing array, so a graph node is one allocation (128 B) instead of five (160 B).
measured_effect: checks-only 35.06M mallocs / 2055 MB -> 33.15M / 2048 MB; typed-app 28.80M -> 27.93M; downlevel-simple 22.59M -> 21.88M mallocs
mech_form: Embed final, never reassigned collection fields (`private final List<X> a = new ArrayList<>(1)`) by value in the owning struct; runtime ArrayList gets a small inline first-element buffer (InitWithBuffer).

subject: perf: SyntacticScopeCreator scans with a scanner on the stack
areas: internal/jscomp syntactic_scope_creator.go; SyntacticScopeCreator.createScope
what: `new ScopeScanner(...).populate()` allocated a heap scanner per created scope; createScope now initialises a stack-local scanner through a shared init function.
measured_effect: checks-only 33.15M mallocs / 2048 MB -> 32.71M / 2020 MB; typed-app 27.93M / 1333 MB -> 27.25M / 1291 MB; downlevel-simple 21.88M -> 21.21M. CPU for this and the three previous commits: checks-only 16.57 s -> 15.05 s, typed-app 10.86 s -> 10.52 s, downlevel-simple 8.59 s -> 8.51 s
mech_form: Emit `new T(args).method()` temporaries (object used for one call chain, never stored) as a stack value initialised by an init function instead of a heap-allocating constructor.

subject: perf: ScopedName.hashCode hashes its scope root without reflection
areas: internal/jscomp scoped_name.go; internal/jutil objects.go (IdentityHashCodeOfPointer)
what: ScopedName.hashCode computed the scope root identity hash via jutil.IdentityHashCode, which boxes into an interface and uses reflection twice; a typed-pointer variant computes the same value directly.
measured_effect: CPU profile downlevel-simple: ScopedNameBase.HashCode 0.14 s -> 0.05 s (1.6% -> 0.6% of samples)
mech_form: Runtime identity-hash helper generic over typed pointers (no `any` boxing, no reflection); translator emits the typed call for System.identityHashCode on a statically typed reference.

subject: perf: build jsgo with profile-guided optimisation (cmd/jsgo/default.pgo)
areas: cmd/jsgo/default.pgo; tools/bench/pgo.py
what: cmd/jsgo is now built with profile-guided optimisation from a merged CPU profile of the benchmark tasks; adds the script that regenerates the profile. No source changes.
measured_effect: without -> with profile, median of 3: downlevel-whitespace 2.64 s -> 2.57 s; downlevel-simple 8.45 s -> 8.10 s; typed-app 10.85 s -> 10.14 s; checks-only 16.35 s -> 15.39 s; 20 single-file compiles x2 11.62 s -> 11.35 s
mech_form: pgo/gc: PGO profile applied at build time; not available to jsgo-mech. The gain is inlining and devirtualisation of hot interface calls (NodeTraversal callbacks, JSType methods); a translator rule emitting direct calls for monomorphic/final receivers is the allowed substitute.

subject: perf: regenerate cmd/jsgo/default.pgo on the v20261015 port
areas: cmd/jsgo/default.pgo
what: Regenerates the PGO profile on the v20261015 port (12 samples instead of 10).
mech_form: pgo/gc: PGO profile applied at build time; not available to jsgo-mech.

what: Round 12 (staged): qualified names are resolved by walking the GETPROP chain (lookup by node, appendQualifiedNameTo into a byte buffer, per-node qname cache) instead of building strings; leaf pre-filters; UnionType slab in the registry.

subject: perf,fix: 64B single-cache-line Node, Pantheon parity fixes, GlobalNamespace tombstones, parallel TypedAst/PrebuildAst/CodePrinter, J2CL/StripCode/ReplaceCssNames reuse
areas: rhino node.go (2040 lines), RhinoStringPool, Token; jscomp TypedAstDeserializer, PrebuildAst parallel, Compiler, CodePrinter, GlobalNamespace, J2CL passes, StripCode, ReplaceCssNames; jutil regex Pattern, EnumSet
what: Shrinks rhino.Node from 80 B to 64 B (pointer-free payload union for string id/number/bigint, all boolean and small-enum props in a 64-bit propFlags, typeOrColor union, cold JSDoc off the hot struct) with a pointer-free 64-shard string pool; adds parallel TypedAst deserialisation, PrebuildAst and chunk code printing; GlobalNamespace ref tombstones; plus Pantheon parity fixes.

mech_form: Node store in the handwritten runtime: 64-byte node record with string ids and float bits in a pointer-free payload word, boolean/enum props as bit flags, type/color in one tagged slot, rare fields in a side box; string pool as open-addressed uint32 table over noscan byte slabs. allowed part also: parallel input parsing that mirrors Java PrebuildAst. Not allowed: parallel CodePrinter/TypedAst decode beyond what Java does, GlobalNamespace tombstones.
notes: No body. Mixed perf + parity-fix commit; the Node/string-pool redesign is the dominant item.

notes: No body; from subject and file list (inferred:). Registry slabs were removed again in fb53b9f5.

subject: perf(jscomp,jutil): unpin TypedAST shards & ColorPool, slab Color.ownProperties, recycle OptimizeCalls/InlineFunctions maps, compact Timeline

notes: No body; from subject and added functions (inferred:).

subject: perf(rhino,jscomp): tag JSType kinds for fast equality/subtype/union dispatch, shrink RhinoStringPool BSS, tag Scope.varHash, fast-path QualifiedName & ScanVars
areas: rhino JSType (kind tag on every concrete type), EqualityChecker, SubtypeChecker, UnionType, ObjectType, QualifiedName, RhinoStringPool, node.go; jscomp Scope (varHash tag), SyntacticScopeCreator ScanVars, NodeTraversal; default.pgo
what: Every concrete JSType gets a kind tag used for fast equality / subtype / union dispatch instead of interface type switches and virtual predicates; string-pool static tables shrunk; Scope.varHash entries carry a hash tag; fast paths in QualifiedName and var scanning.
mech_form: For sealed hierarchies emit a kind byte in the base struct, set by each constructor, and compile instanceof / isX() / visitor dispatch to tag compares and switches on it.
notes: No body; from subject and file list (inferred:). The Scope/QualifiedName fast paths are algorithmic and excluded.

subject: perf(rhino,jscomp): intern Var.nameID (48B->40B), ID-keyed Scope/ReferenceCollector/RemoveUnusedCode/OptimizeCalls lookups, reclaim InferConsts/Normalize local scope arenas, zero-alloc JSType equality pairs, cap slabs <=32KB

subject: perf(compiler): worker node slabs, streaming TypedAST decode, small-span CFG/DFA & parse slices

what: Per-worker Node slabs for parallel parse/deserialise, a streaming reader that decodes large TypedAST shards without loading the whole message, small-span chunking of CFG/DFA flow states, and parse-list slices carved from the ParseArena.

subject: perf(rhino,parsing,jscomp,jutil): eliminate 34.1M heap allocations across staged compilation (Round 2K)
areas: rhino node.go, RhinoStringPool, FunctionType params, JSDocInfo; parsing IRFactory, JsDocInfoParser; jscomp ScriptNodeDeserializer, InlineVariables, MakeDeclaredNamesUnique, GlobalNamespace, CollapseProperties; jutil LinkedHashSet/Map.HashCode; default.pgo
what: Round 2K: CHANGE_TIME inlined in the node payload; cached *string cells; JSDocInfo / JSTypeExpression slab-allocated; allocation-free JSDoc type iterators; stack-allocated LocalVarMotion; no *string boxing in MakeDeclaredNamesUnique; supplier closures guarded; zero-alloc collection HashCode; PGO refresh.
measured_effect: googleapis-bench 97.77 s total; CHECKS 49.98 s / 6013.8 MiB (-277.5 MiB); alloc_objects 121.65M -> 87.51M (-28.1%)
mech_form: Several general rules: lower @Nullable String to string+sentinel instead of *string; emit Supplier/lambda arguments so the closure is only built on the slow path (guarded lazy-message calls); non-escaping iterator objects as stack values; int node props (CHANGE_TIME) as inline fields in the node record (RUNTIME). The JSDoc slabs and source-info template cache are algorithmic and excluded.
notes: Bundle; JSDoc slabs later removed in 904def52.

subject: perf: eliminate 27.1M JSDoc/inliner/chunk/hasher heap allocations (Round 2L)
areas: rhino JSDocInfo iterators; jutil LinkedHashMap.ValueAt, FarmHash hasher; jscomp TypeCheck, CheckSuper, CheckClosureImports, JSTypeColorIdHasher, JSChunk, OptimizeParameters, NodeIterators, FunctionArgumentInjector, FunctionInjector, FunctionToBlockMutator; default.pgo
what: Round 2L: closure-free stack cursor iterators over JSDoc type expressions and parameters; iter.Seq prototype-chain loop replaced by a pointer walk; hasher with inline buffer and Reset reused; immutable GetInputs slice cached; BitSets and scratch maps reused; self-referential pointer removed so stack instances do not escape.
measured_effect: googleapis-bench alloc_objects 87.51M -> 60.39M (-31.0%); CHECKS 47.45M -> 26.52M; bundle-mega 20.93 s / 1311 MB; typed-mega 16.17 s; ~15M iterator/closure/*string allocations removed
mech_form: Emit Java Iterable/Iterator and stream loops as index/cursor loops over the underlying collection instead of iter.Seq closures or heap iterator objects; do not store a self interface pointer in objects that are used as locals (escape); nullable String as value. Scratch reuse in the inliner is algorithmic and excluded.

subject: perf(ast,jscomp): inline unboxed JSDocInfo in Node, nodeExtBox, and CHECKS/OPTIMIZATIONS alloc cuts (Round 2M)
areas: rhino node.go (nodeExtBox, inline JSDocInfo), QualifiedName, TemplateTypeReplacer; parsing JsDocInfoParser; jutil ImmutableMultiset; jscomp TypedAstSerializer, FunctionTypeBuilder, InlineVariables, proto_runtime; default.pgo
what: Round 2M: Node keeps the *JSDocInfo directly in its typeOrColor slot when nothing else is attached and otherwise a nodeExtBox holding type, JSDoc, type-before-cast and cold props; single-token name expressions avoid a builder; QualifiedName join caches; multiset embeds its map by value; packed repeated fields decoded with the reader reused in place.
mech_form: Node store: one tagged pointer slot per node that holds either the type/color, the JSDocInfo, or a pointer to a cold extension box with all rare fields. Protobuf runtime: decode packed repeated fields without a sub-reader allocation.
notes: Body gives no numbers. PGO refresh included.

subject: perf(rhino,jscomp): eliminate 8.5M allocs across JSDoc, JSType, diagnostics, and Stage 2 passes
areas: rhino JSDocInfo builder, JSTypeRegistry slices, PropertyMap, node.go init-from-template; jscomp CollapseProperties (lazy prefix names), InlineCostEstimator, RenameLabels, JSError, DiagnosticType, DependencyInfo, UnionFind; jutil MessageFormat.FormatStrings; colors ColorId; default.pgo

mech_form: algorithmic: mostly per-pass laziness, pooling and pre-checks. allowed part: MessageFormat/DiagnosticType.format with all-String arguments emitted as a ...string call so arguments are not boxed into []any (TRANSLATOR varargs specialisation).
notes: No body; from subject and added functions (inferred:).

subject: perf: streaming proto serde slabs, string-ID polyfill bloom, value AstFactory_Type, and traversal hot-loop optimizations (-6.42M allocs, 95.41s googleapis-bench)
areas: jscomp SerializeTypedAstPass, TypedAstDeserializer, ColorSerializer, proto_runtime, CombinedCompilerPass, NodeTraversal, PolyfillUsageFinder, CollapseProperties, TypeTransformation, AstFactory; jutil BiMap, collections; parsing TypeTransformationParser; default.pgo
